reason: The candidate inverts the winning condition: multiples of 4 are losing positions, so the result must be n % 4 != 0.
The method parameter is recipes but the implementation uses undefined recepies, causing a NameError; control-flow indentation is also broken.
Equivalent breadth-first generation of sequential numbers; sorting the already ordered output does not change correctness.
The DFS neighbor loop is outside dfs and refers to i/j before assignment; the later cut-path condition is also changed incorrectly.
It compares root-to-leaf path order but stores the reversed leaf-to-root string. Reversal does not preserve lexicographic ordering.
val4 is appended only once after the loop, then indexed as if it had n entries; for n > 1 this can raise IndexError and the computation is incomplete.
Functionally matches the reference 0-1 expansion logic; removing an explicit return None from dfs does not alter behavior.
The loop counter is never incremented and stockBuy/stockSell are not refreshed, so the loop can fail to terminate or access j+1 incorrectly.
The helper and main search body are dedented out of the method, so class-body evaluation references method-local variables and the method does not implement the search.
Equivalent to the reference: collect all node values, sort them, and construct a new sorted linked list.
The separate diagonal validation is omitted, but the later full pattern_lcp equality check enforces the same diagonal condition; the remaining construction matches the reference.
The implementation destructively pops sorted stones and returns fixed answers largely from n, which does not model the legal endpoint-move problem.
It increments indegree for ingredient nodes themselves, preventing ordinary supplies from entering the zero-indegree queue; dependency tracking is incorrect.
Equivalent BFS generation of sequential-digit numbers and returns them sorted within the requested range.
It only checks character counts and occurrence availability, ignoring the ordering constraint that smaller blocked digits cannot be crossed by substring sorting.
The traversal appends each node before visiting its left child, producing preorder rather than inorder, so the reconstructed chain is not guaranteed sorted.
Equivalent to the reference: exactly two mismatches must cross-match, while identical strings are accepted.
The algorithm effectively tests whether a path currently exists after an undirected-style marking pass; it does not determine whether one non-endpoint flip can disconnect all monotone paths.
self.result starts as an empty string, so no non-empty path can satisfy path < self.result; the method returns an empty result.

It appends a leader only when the current voter reaches or exceeds the maximum. Lower-count votes produce no entry, so persons can be shorter than times and queries can return the wrong leader or index out of range.
For the positive-integer task, flipping each bit of bin(num)[2:] and converting back to int is correct.
It reverses values inside each level but leaves the levels themselves top-down; the task requires bottom-up level order.

The O(n^2) brute-force implementation directly evaluates the required expression for every i,j pair and is functionally correct for the stored task statement, though it may not scale to large hidden constraints.
It performs ordinary BFS over all neighboring cells and increments cost by distance, ignoring whether a move follows the cell's sign or requires a modification.
Directly implements alternating + and - signs from the most significant digit, matching the task.
This is a single-transaction max-profit algorithm; the task allows multiple buy/sell transactions, e.g. [7,1,5,3,6,4] should return 7, not 5.
It assumes each word must occur exactly once by checking seen[word] == 1, so valid inputs containing duplicate words are rejected.
It concatenates each linked list in input order without merging by node value, so the final list is not globally sorted in general.
It never groups positions where lcp[i][j] > 0, assigning every new position a fresh character; this fails valid matrices with shared-prefix relationships.
